_comment: ASD STIG interview wizard schema. DRAFT — every status-changing action below is a best-effort applicability determination that REQUIRES SME review before use. The wizard JS reads `questions` to render an interview, then resolves `actions` against the blank CKLB skeleton. `rule_groups` are reusable named V-ID sets referenced as "@name". Merge rules: Not_Applicable is dominant; otherwise precedence Not_Applicable > Open > NotAFinding > Not_Reviewed; comments from all matching actions concatenate in question order. `{var}` tokens in comments interpolate the answer with that question/followup id. `always_apply` injects guidance comments without changing status. See README.md for the full schema contract.

system_questions.label: System / application name
system_questions.help: Official name of the application being assessed.

questions.label: Does the application maintain its own user accounts and authentication?
questions.help: Answer No only if the application has no authenticated users at all, OR delegates 100% of authentication and account lifecycle to an external IdP/SSO and holds no local accounts of its own (including admin/service accounts it manages).

actions.comment: The application maintains no local user accounts; account-management, lockout, and account-audit requirements are not applicable. Authentication/account lifecycle is handled outside the application.
No local accounts; shared/group account requirement not applicable.
No local accounts; temporary-account requirement not applicable.
No local accounts; emergency-account requirement not applicable.
Application performs no interactive user logon; DoD logon-banner requirement not applicable. REVIEW: if any interactive logon exists (incl. via SSO redirect), the banner may still be required.
Application performs no local authentication; multifactor-authentication requirements are not applicable to the application (may be inherited from the IdP). REVIEW carefully.

followups.label: Does the application use roles / RBAC for authorization?
followups.text_label: Briefly describe the role model (roles and what each may do).

actions.comment: Role-based access control is implemented. Role model: {roles_used_text}

followups.label: Which of these account kinds does the application actually use?
followups.help: Unchecked kinds let the wizard mark the matching requirement Not Applicable.

actions.comment: Application does not use temporary user accounts; requirement not applicable.
Application does not use emergency accounts; requirement not applicable.
Application does not use shared/group accounts; requirement not applicable.

questions.label: Does the application authenticate users with passwords it manages itself?
questions.help: Answer No if authentication is exclusively CAC/PIV/PKI, or is fully delegated to an external IdP/SSO that owns all password policy.

actions.comment: The application does not manage passwords (authentication is certificate-based and/or delegated to an external identity provider); password-policy requirements are not applicable to the application.

questions.label: Does the application use PKI / certificate-based authentication (CAC, client certs)?

actions.comment: Application does not use PKI-based authentication; certificate path-validation, private-key, identity-mapping, and revocation-cache requirements are not applicable.

Application does not use PKI/PIV credentials for authentication; PIV accept/verify requirements not applicable. REVIEW: DoD generally mandates CAC/PIV — confirm an approved alternative authentication is authorized.

questions.label: Does the application accept identities from OTHER federal agencies or the public (federated / FICAM)?
questions.help: This is about non-organizational, cross-agency, or public federated logins — not your own organization's SSO.

actions.comment: Application serves only organizational users; acceptance/verification of other-agency PIV and FICAM third-party credentials is not applicable.

questions.label: Is the application accessed through a web browser (HTML pages over HTTP/HTTPS)?

actions.comment: Application is not browser-based; HTTP session-cookie and browser-session-identifier requirements are not applicable.
Application renders no HTML to a browser; Cross-Site Scripting and Cross-Site Request Forgery requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Is the application accessible from the public Internet?

actions.comment: Application is not publicly accessible; the publicly-accessible-banner requirement is not applicable (the standard logon banner requirement still applies if there is interactive logon).
Application is not Internet-facing; DMZ requirement may not apply. REVIEW against the actual network architecture.
Application is Internet-accessible — confirm a DMZ separates the DoD enclave from the public network.

questions.label: Does the application use a database?

actions.comment: Application uses no database; SQL-injection, database-object-audit, and database-export requirements are not applicable.
Application uses a database: {uses_database_text}

questions.label: Does the application use SOAP messages, WS-Security, or SAML assertions?

actions.comment: Application does not use SOAP/WS-Security/SAML; SOAP message integrity, WS-Security timestamp, and SAML assertion requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Does the application parse or process XML input?

actions.comment: Application does not process XML; XML-based DoS mitigation and XML-oriented attack requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Is the application a web service / API (SOA), exposing services consumed by other systems?

actions.comment: Application is not a web service / SOA endpoint; service-oriented mutual-TLS, web-service redundancy, and web-service execution-flow requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Does the application deliver or use mobile code (Java applets, ActiveX, Flash/Silverlight, signed downloadable code)?
questions.help: DoD treats applets/ActiveX/Flash as mobile code. Ordinary first-party JavaScript served by your own web app is generally not what these two requirements target — answer No if you use no downloadable/categorized mobile code.

actions.comment: Application uses no categorized/emerging mobile code; mobile-code requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: What is the highest sensitivity of data the application processes?

actions.comment: Application processes only unclassified, non-CUI data; NSA-approved cryptography for classified data, classified-output marking, and Security Classification Guide requirements are not applicable.
Application does not handle multiple classification categories/levels; audit requirements for access/modify/delete of information categories (classification levels) are not applicable.
Application processes classified data — NSA-approved cryptography, output marking, and a Security Classification Guide are required.
Application includes SAMI data — audit trails must be retained for five years.

questions.label: Does the application support remote access sessions (users connecting from outside the local enclave)?

actions.comment: Application does not provide remote access sessions; remote-access encryption and integrity requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Is the application used to perform non-local (remote) maintenance or diagnostic sessions on other systems?
questions.help: This targets management/diagnostic tools, not ordinary application use.

actions.comment: Application is not used for non-local maintenance or diagnostic sessions; the non-local maintenance requirements are not applicable.

questions.label: Is the application transaction-based (performs transactions requiring recovery logs)?

actions.comment: Application is not transaction-based; the transaction-recovery-log requirement is not applicable.

questions.label: Is the software internally developed, GOTS, or COTS / third-party?

actions.comment: COTS/third-party product: code review, code-coverage, coding-standards, design-document, threat-model, defect-tracking, security-tester, SCM/CCB, and developer security-training requirements are the vendor's development-team responsibility, not the fielding organization's. REVIEW: your AO may prefer these documented as inherited/vendor-attested rather than Not Applicable; obtain vendor SDLC artifacts where available.

questions.label: Does the application ITSELF provide centralized audit aggregation, review, reduction, and reporting (as opposed to only forwarding logs to an enterprise SIEM)?
questions.help: Many apps forward to Splunk/ACAS and rely on the SIEM for review/reduction/reporting.

actions.comment: Audit aggregation, review, reduction, and report-generation are provided by the enterprise logging platform (e.g., SIEM), not the application. REVIEW: confirm with your AO — some assessors expect these documented as inherited from the centralized logging service rather than Not Applicable.

always_apply.comment: Configuration management / PPSM control — verify via the application's Configuration Management plan, CM repository controls, PPSM CAL registration, and Application Configuration Guide.
Contingency / backup / fail-secure control — verify against the system Contingency Plan, backup schedule, and recovery procedures.
Patch / vendor-support / decommissioning control — verify the product is vendor-supported, patched current, and has documented update-notification and decommissioning procedures.
ISSO / governance responsibility — verify via system documentation (audit retention/review records, IA violation reporting, change-impact assessments).
General secure-coding / input-handling control — applies to virtually all applications; verify via code review, SAST/DAST results, and testing.
Cryptography / data-protection control — verify FIPS-validated modules and approved encryption are used for data at rest and in transit.

provenance_note: Every action with a status other than Not_Reviewed is an automated applicability determination produced by this wizard and stamped for reviewer attention. An assessor remains responsible for the final determination. Confidence values (high/medium/low) reflect the authoring SME's certainty that the gating question cleanly drives applicability; low-confidence determinations should always be manually confirmed.
